currentContext.strengths: Focused portfolio of five core brands with clear, distinct consumer roles - builds aspiration, pricing power, consumer loyalty and market share|Direct-to-consumer scale across retail and online B2C, giving control over pricing, inventory, merchandising and consumer data|Asset-light retail expansion, predominantly through the FOFO model, with a retail estate spread across 475+ cities and towns|Extensive omnichannel distribution: 1,025 EBOs comprising 13.37 lakh sq. ft. and 9,500+ MBOs and shop-in-shops across department stores|Predominantly India-based sourcing with vendor partnerships and demand-linked planning, reducing response time and inventory risk|Analytics, digital and AI-led decision-making across assortment, pricing, marketing and supply chain|32+ years of retail experience and a supplier base of 100+ suppliers with 10+ warehouses|Proven adjacency playbook - USPA has scaled meaningfully across footwear, kids' wear, innerwear and women's wear
currentContext.strategies: Sharpen a focused five-brand portfolio, each with a distinct consumer role: scale U.S. Polo Assn. as India's leading casual lifestyle brand, position Tommy Hilfiger and Calvin Klein for premiumisation, reimagine Arrow for the Modern Professional consumer, and build Flying Machine as a Gen Z youth brand|Make brands more relevant, distinctive and enduring rather than simply larger|Build the D2C engine by combining physical retail with digital commerce and consumer data into one connected ecosystem; continue investing in larger, more productive store formats|Treat digital as the primary consumer intelligence system rather than a parallel sales channel, becoming a consumer-first rather than channel-first organisation|Invest strategically in data, AI and advanced analytics to improve merchandising, pricing, demand forecasting and customer engagement|Deepen the India-based sourcing model and invest in faster planning, better replenishment, improved inventory lifecycle management and shorter product cycles to stay closer to demand|Maintain disciplined capital allocation and financial discipline while investing ahead of change in future-ready capabilities|Embed the newly articulated Vision, Mission, Values and Ways of Working as operating principles for daily decisions|Treat sustainability as integral to building a business that is resilient, relevant and trusted for the long term|The Company positions management as trustee of shareholders' capital rather than owner, and states that its operations are committed to high levels of operating performance and cost competitiveness, consolidating and building for growth, enhancing the productive asset and resource base and nurturing corporate reputation. It has a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of SEBI LODR, and for FY26 the Board recommended a dividend of Rs 1.60 per fully paid-up equity share of Rs 4 each, to be declared at the AGM. Forward capital-allocation intent is framed around pursuing growth with discipline - mid-double-digit revenue growth, further EBITDA margin expansion, stronger cash flows and continued improvement in ROCE - ensuring that scale is accompanied by profitability, brand strength, inventory freshness and capital efficiency, with continued focus on cost discipline, sourcing agility, selective pricing, inventory control and working capital efficiency. All related party transactions are stated to be on an arm's length basis in the ordinary course of business, with omnibus Audit Committee approval for foreseen and repetitive transactions.|'Combat Climate Change' is maintained as a formal sustainability pillar under which energy-efficiency and renewable-energy initiatives are grouped|Approximately 5% of energy consumed during FY 2026 came from renewable sources|Conventional lighting has been replaced with LED across stores and warehouses; 690 light fittings were replaced with LED at the Bangalore corporate office and CFL fittings in the guest house were replaced with LED|Motion-sensor LED lights installed for warehouse energy management in FY25 indicated a 5%-8% reduction potential in energy demand; the same is being evaluated and implemented for upcoming new warehouses|The state-of-the-art warehouse facility at Hoskote, Karnataka is undertaking the procedures for Green Building Certification|A wheeled-solar-power agreement signed with an independent power producer in FY19 for a period of 9 years is expected to cover 80-95% of the corporate office energy demand, with potential to mitigate ~1,030 tons of carbon dioxide annually|The Company is exploring shifting its warehouses to renewable energy, with preliminary rooftop-solar surveys conducted by external agencies|The Company is engaging vendor partners to enable their transition to renewable energy, to reduce the overall carbon footprint of its products|Zero-tolerance policy on sexual harassment with an independently functioning Internal Complaints Committee and formally trained members; no incidences of sexual harassment were reported during FY 2025-26|A Risk Management Committee of four Non-Executive Directors plus the Managing Director & CEO oversees risk; all Committee recommendations made during the year were accepted by the Board
currentContext.expansion: Arvind Fashions expanded its retail footprint during FY2025-26 while maintaining the discipline of an asset-light model - the Company does not describe any manufacturing capex. Net square footage addition for the year was approximately 1.43 lakh square feet, a meaningful acceleration from the 1.22 lakh square feet added in the prior year, with store expansion continuing predominantly through the FOFO (franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated) model consistent with the Company's asset-light philosophy. The retail estate is distributed across 475+ cities and towns, with growing penetration of Tier II and Tier III markets where branded fashion aspiration is rising alongside improvements in disposable income and urban infrastructure. As of March 31, 2026 the network comprised 1,025 EBOs totalling 13.37 lakh sq. ft., 9,500+ MBOs and shop-in-shops across department stores, and 10+ warehouses. Investment continued during the year in new and differentiated retail formats, including the 'Club A' concept offering an elevated brand experience and 'Stride', the innovative footwear specialty format. Digital commerce was the other expansion vector, with online B2C revenue growing 45% during FY2025-26 on the back of digital assortment, marketplace partnerships and owned-platform capabilities, while USPA scaled the adjacency strategy across footwear, kids' wear, innerwear and women's wear. On the corporate-structure side, the Company acquired Flipkart India Private Limited's full 31.25% fully-diluted stake in Arvind Youth Brands Private Limited, which became a wholly owned subsidiary (direct and indirect holding) as on December 29, 2025. Management notes cost pressure on select raw materials, shipping and capex arising from the geopolitical situation.
currentContext.mdna: Indian fashion consumption is shifting towards quality and experience-led choices, with mid-premium and premium apparel emerging as among the fastest-growing segments - a trend that aligns directly with the portfolio being built|Management expects to sustain mid-double-digit revenue growth and deliver further EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, while continuing to invest in marketing, technology, AI, people and strategic capability|India's continuing premiumisation journey makes the portfolio of globally admired and homegrown brands a meaningful platform for sustained growth|The D2C engine, at 56% of total sales (+270 bps year-on-year), is compounding with every passing quarter as physical retail, digital commerce and consumer data combine|Like-for-like retail growth of 8.1%, consistent through the year, is being driven by continued investment in larger, more productive store formats|Quality-of-growth levers cited: fresher inventory, healthier gross margins, improving capital efficiency and better full-price sell-through|Technology, AI, advanced analytics and digital ecosystems will increasingly determine the speed, intelligence and precision with which fashion companies compete|Headwinds acknowledged: geopolitical developments, changing trade dynamics, inflationary pressures, technological disruption and shifting consumer expectations will continue to test businesses

risks.note: Management states that because of the geo-political situation multiple industries are facing shortages in petroleum-derived products, especially natural gas which is a key input for production, exposing the Company's sourcing base to supply disruption.
The Company reports it is witnessing an impact on the rupee, and it runs foreign-currency expenditure alongside much smaller foreign-currency earnings, so a weaker rupee raises landed input cost.

risks.risk: Raw material, shipping and capex cost inflation
risks.note: Management flags pressure on prices of select raw materials, shipping and capex, which compresses gross margin and raises the cost of the store-expansion programme.
The Directors' Report states consumption has slowed down due to supply-led inflationary pressure - a direct threat to discretionary apparel volumes and to like-for-like retail growth.

Retail growth continues predominantly through the FOFO model across 475+ cities and towns, so store additions, working capital and execution quality depend on franchise partners rather than owned assets.

risks.risk: Concentration in a single discretionary category and geography
risks.note: The business is a single-activity branded apparel and lifestyle platform serving Indian consumers through five core brands; there is no diversification away from Indian discretionary fashion demand.

one-line thesis: FY27 opened with the strongest quarter in the current cycle — 15.5% revenue growth, 19.6% EBITDA growth and a 90bps gross-margin gain driven by full-price sell-through, not discounting. The structural story is the channel pivot: direct channels are now 62% of sales (+380bps YoY), which management explicitly frames as owning the customer, the experience and the margin. Reported PAT fell (INR10cr vs INR13cr) purely on lower other income — a base effect from last year's Ind AS 116 lease-unwind gains on COCO closures, not an operating miss.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (NSV) | INR1,279 cr | +15.5% (vs INR1,107 cr) | LFL retail 11.6%; retail +18%; online B2C +38% |
| EBITDA / margin | INR160 cr (ex other income) | +19.6% (vs INR133 cr); margin +44bps | After absorbing ~50bps higher marketing spend |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | ~INR10 cr | vs INR13 cr — down | Decline entirely from lower other income; operating performance strong |
| Gross margin | 56.7% | +~90bps | From full-price sell-through, lower discounting, channel mix to direct |
| Order book | n/a (retail model) | — | SS27 buying commitments due over next 45–60 days |
| Cash / net debt | not disclosed on call | — | NWC days stable; inventory turn ~3.5x |

> Adjustments / one-offs: (a) Other income fell because Q1 FY26 carried Ind AS 116 unwind gains on a large number of COCO store closures — normalized run-rate now INR7–8 cr/quarter. (b) Minority interest is now purely the PVH JV share (Flying Machine minority gone after residual-stake buyout), so PAT optics understate 100%-owned brand profit. (c) Post-Ind AS vs pre-Ind AS PAT differential is 4–5%. (d) Inventory +3 days QoQ / receivables −2 days QoQ — mix-driven (400bps channel shift ≈ 6 days extra inventory) plus early PVH inward.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** "confident of sustaining **mid-double-digit revenue growth in the balance of the year**"; separately reaffirmed **12–15% growth for FY27**, with LFL vs new-store (inorganic) contribution split roughly **50:50**.
- **Margin:** **30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion** for FY27. Management notes 200bps of margin expansion already delivered over the last two years.
- **Order book / inflow target:** n/a. Other income guided **stable at ~INR7–8 cr/quarter**.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** **1.5 lakh net sq ft** retail area addition in FY27 (gross adds against a standing ~5% annual closure rate). **Flying Machine dotcom + app to launch in H2 FY27**. Inventory turn to improve from **3.5x to 3.7–3.8x within 18–24 months**.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxy is the buying calendar: SS27 sourcing commitments are to be locked over the next 45–60 days, and management said explicitly that if raw-material and fuel prices remain at current (West Asia conflict-inflated) levels at that point, "we will be forced to take some kind of pricing correction." The long inventory cycle has so far insulated the P&L from input inflation — that shield expires with the SS27 buy.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **U.S. Polo Association** — led the portfolio with "exceptional growth" on a high Q1 FY26 base. Largest network, deeply penetrated across ~150 cities. Deliberate extra inventory placed in the brand is capturing incremental demand. Strategy is upsizing rather than pure store-count growth: larger stores are clocking the *same* PSFPD as smaller ones, so revenue scales with square footage.
- **PVH brands (Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein)** — "back on growth" after absorbing GST changes on premium apparel. CK targets households above INR50 lakh income. Both restricted to Grade-A malls.
- **Flying Machine** — double-digit growth since the residual-stake acquisition; repositioned as a Gen-Z, denim-core, unisex brand; now live across multiple e-com platforms; dotcom/app in H2. Smallest of the three main fleets — "significant headroom." Store strategy is "centre of culture" (youth/university catchments), not blanket expansion.
- **Arrow** — delivering through wholesale; being pivoted to "the modern professional." Current focus is efficiency and profitability first, direct-channel strengthening (store formats, renovations, merchandising) second, marketing push only after that.
- **Channel mix** — direct 62% of sales (+380bps YoY); online B2C share 18% vs 15% LY; deliberate pivot *away* from B2B online. Wholesale and department stores still delivered strong double-digit secondary sales. 23 EBOs added gross in the quarter.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Data/AI/analytics as a central capability** — organisation restructured into brand-owned business units with revenue P&L pushed into brands, while marketing, digital, data and AI were *centralised* to create leverage across the portfolio. Restructuring is complete. Early results already visible in discount optimisation and pricing.
- **Consumer landscape study completed** — produced a "clear road map of the market opportunity," now shaping where-to-play choices. Conclusion drawn: casual lifestyle is the fastest-growing offtake pool and the portfolio sits squarely in it.
- **U.S. Polo footwear** — riding the sneaker/all-day-comfort category off the brand halo; BIS-driven availability constraint of last year now resolved.
- **Closer-to-market supply chain** — shortening lead cycles to catch trend shifts (e.g. linen demand); explicitly *not* framed as fast fashion. Expected to release inventory efficiency over time.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Owned distribution economics.** 62% direct share means the company controls pricing, assortment and discounting — evidenced by gross margin rising 90bps *while* discounting fell and marketing spend rose 50bps.
- **Brand portfolio breadth across price ladders.** Management evidenced share gain specifically inside multi-brand environments: "when we compare ourselves in a more multi-brand environment, we are gaining share," with department-store and MBO secondary sales growing double-digit — i.e. outgrowing the rest of those platforms' portfolios.
- **Upsizing economics.** Larger U.S. Polo stores hold PSFPD flat while adding footage — a rare retail result and the reason area addition (1.5 lakh sq ft), not door count, is the growth metric.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin +90bps to 56.7% attributed to three stacked drivers: premiumization/product mix, lower discounting (higher full-price sell-through), and channel mix toward retail/online B2C which structurally yields higher GM. Below GP, costs rose from a multi-state wage hike and channel-expansion-linked operating costs, plus a deliberate ~50bps step-up in marketing investment — yet EBITDA margin still expanded 44bps, which management reads as operating leverage. Input pressure (West Asia conflict on raw material, fuel, forex) has *not* yet hit COGS because of the long inventory cycle. Management was explicit that the GM gain was NOT from carrying cheap old inventory.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 target: **1.5 lakh net square feet** added. Q1 delivered 23 gross EBO adds against a net of ~4–5 — closures run at a structural ~5% of fleet annually, part performance pruning and part upsizing churn.
- U.S. Polo: upsizing/renovation of existing catchments is the primary lever; new catchments opportunistic.
- Flying Machine: selective store openings in youth catchments + right-sized boxes with new retail identity; existing fleet to be sifted.
- Arrow: box-size review and upsizing; present in 80–90 cities.
- Digital: Flying Machine dotcom and app in H2 FY27 — a dated, checkable milestone.
capital allocation: Investment is being directed at (i) brand marketing (deliberately raised 50bps), (ii) analytics/technology/AI and the talent to run it, and (iii) retail footprint expansion and upsizing. Working capital: inventory has structurally shifted onto the balance sheet as the channel mix moved direct, offset by falling receivables — management guided that the two "will both balance each other out" sequentially. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary on this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **West Asia conflict** — flagged repeatedly as the live macro risk: supply lines, raw material, fuel prices and forex. Explicitly a "watch item."
- **SS27 pricing decision (next 45–60 days)** — if input prices don't normalise, a price increase is likely. Watch whether the 30–40bps margin guidance survives it.
- **Inventory build ahead of demand** — inventory is up on channel-mix logic *plus* pre-emptive PVH sourcing shifted for geopolitical risk. If H2 demand softens, FCF is exposed. Management's answer was cost control first, pricing action only "if required."
- **PAT optics** — a stronger PVH JV raises minority interest, so consolidated PAT growth will keep lagging EBITDA growth.
- **Early EOSS across the industry** — competitors starting end-of-season sales earlier and mid-season discounting is visible; a discounting war would directly attack the full-price-sell-through thesis.
- **Wage inflation across multiple states** — structural, already in the cost base.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific. Amisha Jain gave numeric guidance unprompted (mid-double-digit growth, 30–40bps margin) and reaffirmed the 12–15% FY27 number under questioning rather than hedging. Girdhar Chitlangia was disciplined about pointing analysts to the *sequential* read on working capital rather than defending the YoY optics, and pre-committed to the two metrics balancing out — a checkable claim. Notably the team declined to disclose the full-price-sell-through percentage directly, redirecting to the gross margin outcome. On AI they stayed honest: "very early days, early results," no quantified benefit claimed.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The org redesign is the real story under the numbers: revenue P&L moved *into* brands (accountability) while data/AI/marketing moved *out* to the centre (leverage). That is a deliberate bet that consumer analytics is a shared asset, not a brand-level one.
- Larger stores holding PSFPD constant is the quiet unlock — it means area addition converts almost linearly to revenue, which is why guidance is given in square feet rather than store count.
- Flying Machine's minority interest disappearing changes the PAT bridge: any future minority drag is now *purely* a read on PVH's performance, i.e. rising minority interest is a bullish signal for the premium portfolio.
- Management refused the "fast fashion" framing while adopting its core mechanic (closer-to-market drops) — a positioning choice, since fast fashion implies disposable product that would dilute brand equity.

- **Upsizing economics.** Larger U.S. Polo stores hold PSFPD flat while adding footage — a rare retail result and the reason area addition (1.5 lakh sq ft), not door count, is the growth metric.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin +90bps to 56.7% attributed to three stacked drivers: premiumization/product mix, lower discounting (higher full-price sell-through), and channel mix toward retail/online B2C which structurally yields higher GM. Below GP, costs rose from a multi-state wage hike and channel-expansion-linked operating costs, plus a deliberate ~50bps step-up in marketing investment — yet EBITDA margin still expanded 44bps, which management reads as operating leverage. Input pressure (West Asia conflict on raw material, fuel, forex) has *not* yet hit COGS because of the long inventory cycle. Management was explicit that the GM gain was NOT from carrying cheap old inventory.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 target: **1.5 lakh net square feet** added. Q1 delivered 23 gross EBO adds against a net of ~4–5 — closures run at a structural ~5% of fleet annually, part performance pruning and part upsizing churn.
- U.S. Polo: upsizing/renovation of existing catchments is the primary lever; new catchments opportunistic.
- Flying Machine: selective store openings in youth catchments + right-sized boxes with new retail identity; existing fleet to be sifted.
- Arrow: box-size review and upsizing; present in 80–90 cities.
- Digital: Flying Machine dotcom and app in H2 FY27 — a dated, checkable milestone.
capital allocation: Investment is being directed at (i) brand marketing (deliberately raised 50bps), (ii) analytics/technology/AI and the talent to run it, and (iii) retail footprint expansion and upsizing. Working capital: inventory has structurally shifted onto the balance sheet as the channel mix moved direct, offset by falling receivables — management guided that the two "will both balance each other out" sequentially. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary on this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **West Asia conflict** — flagged repeatedly as the live macro risk: supply lines, raw material, fuel prices and forex. Explicitly a "watch item."
- **SS27 pricing decision (next 45–60 days)** — if input prices don't normalise, a price increase is likely. Watch whether the 30–40bps margin guidance survives it.
- **Inventory build ahead of demand** — inventory is up on channel-mix logic *plus* pre-emptive PVH sourcing shifted for geopolitical risk. If H2 demand softens, FCF is exposed. Management's answer was cost control first, pricing action only "if required."
- **PAT optics** — a stronger PVH JV raises minority interest, so consolidated PAT growth will keep lagging EBITDA growth.
- **Early EOSS across the industry** — competitors starting end-of-season sales earlier and mid-season discounting is visible; a discounting war would directly attack the full-price-sell-through thesis.
- **Wage inflation across multiple states** — structural, already in the cost base.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific. Amisha Jain gave numeric guidance unprompted (mid-double-digit growth, 30–40bps margin) and reaffirmed the 12–15% FY27 number under questioning rather than hedging. Girdhar Chitlangia was disciplined about pointing analysts to the *sequential* read on working capital rather than defending the YoY optics, and pre-committed to the two metrics balancing out — a checkable claim. Notably the team declined to disclose the full-price-sell-through percentage directly, redirecting to the gross margin outcome. On AI they stayed honest: "very early days, early results," no quantified benefit claimed.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The org redesign is the real story under the numbers: revenue P&L moved *into* brands (accountability) while data/AI/marketing moved *out* to the centre (leverage). That is a deliberate bet that consumer analytics is a shared asset, not a brand-level one.
- Larger stores holding PSFPD constant is the quiet unlock — it means area addition converts almost linearly to revenue, which is why guidance is given in square feet rather than store count.
- Flying Machine's minority interest disappearing changes the PAT bridge: any future minority drag is now *purely* a read on PVH's performance, i.e. rising minority interest is a bullish signal for the premium portfolio.
- Management refused the "fast fashion" framing while adopting its core mechanic (closer-to-market drops) — a positioning choice, since fast fashion implies disposable product that would dilute brand equity.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

hero.oneLiner: One of India's leading branded apparel and lifestyle companies, running a focused portfolio of five iconic global and homegrown brands through an asset-light, increasingly direct-to-consumer omnichannel model.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's leading branded apparel and lifestyle companies, running a focused portfolio of five iconic global and homegrown brands through an asset-light, increasingly direct-to-consumer omnichannel model.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Arvind Fashions Limited builds and operates a focused portfolio of global and homegrown fashion brands - U.S. Polo Assn., Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Arrow and Flying Machine - addressing casualwear, premium fashion, denim, workwear, innerwear, footwear, kidswear, womenswear and accessories. Its business model is built around brand strength, design and merchandising capability, sourcing excellence, retail execution, direct-to-consumer growth, omnichannel presence and asset-light scalability. Products reach consumers through Exclusive Brand Outlets, multi-brand outlets, department stores, online marketplaces, brand websites and digital platforms across 475+ cities and towns.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Arvind Lifestyle Brands Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding per Form AOC-1); counterparty for shared services, guarantee commission, interest income and investments
- PVH Arvind Fashion Private Limited — JV: Subsidiary described in Form AOC-1 as a controlled entity jointly owned with PVH BV; 50% shareholding
- Arvind Youth Brands Private Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary Company of Arvind Lifestyle Brands Limited; 39.60% shareholding shown in Form AOC-1; the Company also holds Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares in it
- Value Fashion Retail Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary Company of Arvind Lifestyle Brands Limited; 100% shareholding per Form AOC-1
- Arvind Limited — related party: Enterprise on which a Non-Executive Director exercises significant influence; provider of shared services
- Arvind Smart Textile Limited — related party: Enterprise on which a Non-Executive Director exercises significant influence
- Arvind Envisol Limited — related party: Enterprise on which a Non-Executive Director exercises significant influence; provider of shared services
- Aura Securities Private Limited — related party: Entity with Significant Influence over the Company; recipient of dividend
- Aura Merchandise Private Limited — related party: Enterprise on which a Non-Executive Director exercises significant influence; recipient of dividend
- Atul Limited — related party: Enterprise on which a Non-Executive Director exercises significant influence; recipient of dividend

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **U.S. Polo Association** — led the portfolio with "exceptional growth" on a high Q1 FY26 base. Largest network, deeply penetrated across ~150 cities. Deliberate extra inventory placed in the brand is capturing incremental demand. Strategy is upsizing rather than pure store-count growth: larger stores are clocking the *same* PSFPD as smaller ones, so revenue scales with square footage.
- **PVH brands (Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein)** — "back on growth" after absorbing GST changes on premium apparel. CK targets households above INR50 lakh income. Both restricted to Grade-A malls.
- **Flying Machine** — double-digit growth since the residual-stake acquisition; repositioned as a Gen-Z, denim-core, unisex brand; now live across multiple e-com platforms; dotcom/app in H2. Smallest of the three main fleets — "significant headroom." Store strategy is "centre of culture" (youth/university catchments), not blanket expansion.
- **Arrow** — delivering through wholesale; being pivoted to "the modern professional." Current focus is efficiency and profitability first, direct-channel strengthening (store formats, renovations, merchandising) second, marketing push only after that.
- **Channel mix** — direct 62% of sales (+380bps YoY); online B2C share 18% vs 15% LY; deliberate pivot *away* from B2B online. Wholesale and department stores still delivered strong double-digit secondary sales. 23 EBOs added gross in the quarter.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Brands:** U.S. Polo Assn., Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Arrow, Flying Machine
- **Categories:** Casualwear, Premium fashion, Denim, Workwear, Innerwear, Footwear, Kidswear, Womenswear, Accessories
- **Retail formats:** Exclusive Brand Outlets, 'Club A' elevated brand-experience concept, 'Stride' footwear specialty format

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India - premium, mid-premium and youth fashion consumers across categories, occasions and generations
- 475+ cities and towns, with growing penetration of Tier II and Tier III markets
- Organised retail: Exclusive Brand Outlets, large format stores, multi-brand outlets and department stores
- Online B2C - brand websites, owned digital platforms and leading online marketplaces

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxy is the buying calendar: SS27 sourcing commitments are to be locked over the next 45–60 days, and management said explicitly that if raw-material and fuel prices remain at current (West Asia conflict-inflated) levels at that point, "we will be forced to take some kind of pricing correction." The long inventory cycle has so far insulated the P&L from input inflation — that shield expires with the SS27 buy.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** "confident of sustaining **mid-double-digit revenue growth in the balance of the year**"; separately reaffirmed **12–15% growth for FY27**, with LFL vs new-store (inorganic) contribution split roughly **50:50**.
- **Margin:** **30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion** for FY27. Management notes 200bps of margin expansion already delivered over the last two years.
- **Order book / inflow target:** n/a. Other income guided **stable at ~INR7–8 cr/quarter**.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** **1.5 lakh net sq ft** retail area addition in FY27 (gross adds against a standing ~5% annual closure rate). **Flying Machine dotcom + app to launch in H2 FY27**. Inventory turn to improve from **3.5x to 3.7–3.8x within 18–24 months**.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Data/AI/analytics as a central capability** — organisation restructured into brand-owned business units with revenue P&L pushed into brands, while marketing, digital, data and AI were *centralised* to create leverage across the portfolio. Restructuring is complete. Early results already visible in discount optimisation and pricing.
- **Consumer landscape study completed** — produced a "clear road map of the market opportunity," now shaping where-to-play choices. Conclusion drawn: casual lifestyle is the fastest-growing offtake pool and the portfolio sits squarely in it.
- **U.S. Polo footwear** — riding the sneaker/all-day-comfort category off the brand halo; BIS-driven availability constraint of last year now resolved.
- **Closer-to-market supply chain** — shortening lead cycles to catch trend shifts (e.g. linen demand); explicitly *not* framed as fast fashion. Expected to release inventory efficiency over time.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian fashion consumption is shifting towards quality and experience-led choices, with mid-premium and premium apparel emerging as among the fastest-growing segments - a trend that aligns directly with the portfolio being built
- Management expects to sustain mid-double-digit revenue growth and deliver further EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, while continuing to invest in marketing, technology, AI, people and strategic capability
- India's continuing premiumisation journey makes the portfolio of globally admired and homegrown brands a meaningful platform for sustained growth
- The D2C engine, at 56% of total sales (+270 bps year-on-year), is compounding with every passing quarter as physical retail, digital commerce and consumer data combine
- Like-for-like retail growth of 8.1%, consistent through the year, is being driven by continued investment in larger, more productive store formats
- Quality-of-growth levers cited: fresher inventory, healthier gross margins, improving capital efficiency and better full-price sell-through
- Technology, AI, advanced analytics and digital ecosystems will increasingly determine the speed, intelligence and precision with which fashion companies compete
- Headwinds acknowledged: geopolitical developments, changing trade dynamics, inflationary pressures, technological disruption and shifting consumer expectations will continue to test businesses

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Arvind Fashions expanded its retail footprint during FY2025-26 while maintaining the discipline of an asset-light model - the Company does not describe any manufacturing capex. Net square footage addition for the year was approximately 1.43 lakh square feet, a meaningful acceleration from the 1.22 lakh square feet added in the prior year, with store expansion continuing predominantly through the FOFO (franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated) model consistent with the Company's asset-light philosophy. The retail estate is distributed across 475+ cities and towns, with growing penetration of Tier II and Tier III markets where branded fashion aspiration is rising alongside improvements in disposable income and urban infrastructure. As of March 31, 2026 the network comprised 1,025 EBOs totalling 13.37 lakh sq. ft., 9,500+ MBOs and shop-in-shops across department stores, and 10+ warehouses. Investment continued during the year in new and differentiated retail formats, including the 'Club A' concept offering an elevated brand experience and 'Stride', the innovative footwear specialty format. Digital commerce was the other expansion vector, with online B2C revenue growing 45% during FY2025-26 on the back of digital assortment, marketplace partnerships and owned-platform capabilities, while USPA scaled the adjacency strategy across footwear, kids' wear, innerwear and women's wear. On the corporate-structure side, the Company acquired Flipkart India Private Limited's full 31.25% fully-diluted stake in Arvind Youth Brands Private Limited, which became a wholly owned subsidiary (direct and indirect holding) as on December 29, 2025. Management notes cost pressure on select raw materials, shipping and capex arising from the geopolitical situation.
